title: Restaurant & Catering (FOH) Supervisor, #26-069
description:
Are you the ultimate TEAM player who is ready to lead a team? Join Naval Academy Hospitality and work with an outstanding group of professionals to support our varied catering events. From weddings, to retirements, class reunions, Midshipmen Events, and conferences, we cover it all! Our Retail Dining FOH Supervisors get to work in a variety of locations spanning from Catering, to our signature coffee shop 1845, the Alley Restaurant and our outdoor bars for various USNA sporting events. We are looking for highly professional individuals that love to keep moving and provide a welcoming atmosphere for our guests while making their experience on the Yard one to remember.

Applications must be submitted by NOON on September 21, 2026 to be considered for this position.

In order to meet the basic requirement of the Retail Dining FOH Supervisor position, NF-1101-03, you must meet one of the following requirements:

  1. Possess one (1) year of specialized experience in a food service role that equipped you to perform successfully the duties of this position. Specialized experience may include, but is not limited to: Front of House, Back of House, supervisory/managerial duties in the food service industry; OR
  2. five (5) years of education beyond high school; OR
  3. have three (3) years of general work experience.

You will be rated on the following Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) for this position:

  1. Ability to independently lead FOH teams, oversee shift assignments (setup, service, teardown), and execute operations in full compliance with SOPs and BEOs.
  2. Experience providing proactive guest engagement during events and rapidly resolving service, food, or beverage complaints.
  3. Knowledge of dining, bar, and barista operations, including strict health/sanitation compliance and alcohol awareness. Preferred Education in Hotel & Restaurant Management or related field.
  4. Ability to communicate clearly across diverse teams and coordinate seamless execution between FOH, kitchen, catering, and logistics staff.
  5. Experience overseeing and completing inventory management, post-event revenue collection, post-event administrative reports.

JOB SUMMARY

The Retail Dining FOH (Front of the House) Supervisor position is located in the U. S. Naval Academy's Non-Appropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI), Naval Academy Business Services Division (NABSD), Annapolis, Maryland. NAFI is an entity that generates its own funds through its operations, and is not funded by Congress. The FOH Supervisor supervises day-of a la carte operations, which includes on-site FOH staff, set-up, execution, and tear down of the operation/event. The Retail Dining FOH Supervisor stays in contact with the host (on-site contact) and/or member/guest to ensure the highest guest satisfaction possible. All duties are to be performed in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, as well as NABSD Retail Dining and Hospitality policies, practices and procedures.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Execute day-to-day operations for designated la carte locations according to Manager specification, and location specific SOPs. Execute banquet events according to Banquet Event Order specifications.
  • Oversee/prepare staff assignments to include set-up, service, tear-down and side work. Confirms all FOH service staff are in proper uniform, presenting a clean and professional image.
  • Communicate with Managers, kitchen, logistics, and inventory staff to coordinate execution according to specifications. Confirms reservations for The Alley restaurant and Member featured events as needed; Communicates floor plans (setup of tables, chairs, linens, table settings, etc.) and ensures room preparation is accurate. Maintains safe, secure, legal, and healthy work environment, enforcing sanitation, quality of food preparation, service standards and procedures; conforming to the regulations of the alcoholic beverage commission.
  • Acknowledge, greet, and thank all members and guests, and ensure client satisfaction by communicating with the members/guests. Investigate and resolve complaints regarding food and beverage quality and/or service, within scope of authority; otherwise refer the matter to appropriate management for resolution.
  • Maintains ambiance by controlling lighting, background music, linen service, glassware, dinnerware, utensil quality and placement; monitoring customer facing chill boxes, merchandisers, and condiment counters; monitoring food presentation and service. Assist FOH/BOH staff by refilling drinks, delivering food, bussing tables, bar support, barista support, etc. Settle cash bars, manage revenue, and manage inventory by properly completing banquet post-function reports, bar inventory sheets, and a la carte inventory sheet (in accordance with SOPs) at the conclusion of the event. Adhere to sanitation, safety and alcohol beverage control policies including confirming legal drinking age and discontinuing service to intoxicated guests. Must understand and be able to train on alcohol awareness procedures such as proper pouring, accountability and proper cut off procedures. Must be C.A.R.E Trained.
  • The work requires the use of arms, hands and legs and involves prolonged standing, walking, reaching, and light lifting. Objects handled and carried may weigh in excess of 20 pounds.

QUALIFICATIONS & CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT

Applicants who meet the qualification requirements will be further evaluated to determine the extent to which their education, related experience, training, awards, and supervisory appraisal demonstrate they possess the desired knowledge, skills, and abilities (KSAs).

  • Must obtain and maintain a secret security clearance – requires 18 years of age
  • Males born after December 31, 1959 must be registered for Selective Service

  • Reference Checks

  • Must maintain the privacy of official work information and data, and demonstrate the highest level of ethical conduct.

title: 2027 Summer Technology Internal Audit Internship- Remote
description:
Location:

For Those Who Work At Home, Ohio

Summer 2027 Technology Audit Internship- Remote

What does our Internship Program offer?

Key’s Enterprise Internship is a 10.5-week program that provides meaningful work that matters, offers feedback and coaching, and creates engaging events and conversations that will spark excitement and interest in bringing one’s full-time career to Key.

Interns are involved in a host of line of business specific projects that directly impact and benefit Key’s business and strategic pillars. The program includes networking with Key teammates across all levels of the organization, a series of Learning Labs where internal and external speakers provide insight on Key’s competitive landscape, financial wellness, and professional development best practices, and an assigned mentor who shares knowledge, experience, and advice.

Internal Audit

The internal audit function within KeyBank provides an independent assessment on Key’s processes and risks. As a trusted advisor, the Internal Audit tests the adequacy and effectiveness of KeyBank’s risk management practices, makes recommendations for improvement, and monitors remediation efforts. Internal Audit is accountable to the KeyCorp Audit Committee and reporting is provided to key stakeholders, including the Board of Directors and associated committees, executive and line of business management, and KeyBank’s regulators.

About the Internal Audit Internship Program

As an Internal Audit Technology Intern, you will gain experience working on various technology audits, work closely with seasoned professionals to develop your skills as an auditor and technology professional while receiving direct coaching and feedback. Interns will have exposure to various lines of business across Key and interact with their leaders. Placement for Technology Internal Audit Interns may be in one or more of the following areas: Information Security, Technology Services, Applications Audit, Project Audit or IT General Controls.

Internal Audit operates in a remote work environment with teammates located in over 20 states. Your internship will be performed in a virtual environment; however, if you are located close to Buffalo, NY or Cleveland, OH, you may have the option to occasionally work in an office setting.

Based on performance, Interns may be offered the opportunity for placement in a full-time position as a Rotational Analyst with Internal Audit upon graduation.

Job Responsibilities

  • Staffed on one or two technology audits allowing you to gain insight into all phases of an audit (planning, fieldwork, and reporting) and learn about various parts of the organization.
  • Internal Audit follows an annual Audit Plan and work assigned each week will be based on the current reviews in process on your assigned team.
  • Perform research to understand the technology risks associated with the audit.
  • Typically work 8-hour days, Interns are not expected to work more than 40 hours/week
  • Attend audit specific training and enterprise-wide Learning Labs.
  • Network with other Internal Audit Interns & members of Internal Audit’s Senior Leadership Team (senior management).
  • Internship culminates with a Spotlight presentation to Senior Leadership Team and Managers in Internal Audit highlighting your internship experience.

Qualifications

  • Must have completed at least three years toward a four-year, undergraduate degree program with coursework in Information Systems, Computer Science, Accounting, Finance, Economics, Project management or other business or technology related degrees, with an anticipated graduation date in or before May 2028.
  • Outstanding academic achievement (minimum undergraduate 3.25 GPA)
  • Demonstrated leadership and teamwork from past work experience and/or extracurricular activities
  • Strong interest in technology
  • Solid analytical, problem solving, communication (oral & written) and presentation skills
  • Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint

Compensation and Benefits

This position is eligible to earn an hourly rate of $23 per hour. Compensation also includes a $2,000 Summer Internship Sign-on Bonus.

Classification

Pipeline Safety Inspector I

Class Definition

GENERAL STATEMENT OF DUTIES: To assist with inspections of natural gas pipeline facilities (such as standard, construction, and follow-up inspections) including inspecting and observing critical valves, regulator stations, master meters, relief valves, pressure recorders, odorizers, and rectifiers using Field Evaluation forms; to utilize specialized equipment such as multi-meters and odorometers; to follow applicable guidelines and regulations, supervisory directives, and professional standards in order to determine compliance with state and federal regulations regarding design, installation, operation, and maintenance of facilities; and to do related work as required.

SUPERVISION RECEIVED: Works under the general direction of a superior with latitude for the exercise of independent judgement in technical and administrative matters; work is reviewed for conformance to Division policies and industry regulations.

SUPERVISION EXERCISED: Usually none.

ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLES OF WORK PERFORMED:

  • To assist with inspections of natural gas pipeline facilities (such as standard, construction, and follow-up inspections) including inspecting and observing critical valves, regulator stations, master meters, relief valves, pressure recorders, odorizers, and rectifiers using Field Evaluation forms.
  • To utilize specialized equipment such as multi-meters and odorometers.
  • To follow applicable guidelines and regulations, supervisory directives, and professional standards in order to determine compliance with state and federal regulations regarding design, installation, operation, and maintenance of facilities.
  • To review natural gas operators’ programs, plans, procedures, policies, maps, records and other documents necessary to determine compliance with federal and state statutes and regulations.
  • To assist in conducting pipeline safety evaluations as well as incident and accident investigations.
  • To assist in the inspection of gas pipeline facilities such as regulator stations, leak repairs, relief valves, rectifiers, odorizers, master meters, and critical valves in order to ensure safety and compliance with state and federal regulations.
  • To assist in inspecting gas pipelines during construction including reviewing welding procedures, plastic joining procedures, and use of proper materials in order to ensure safety and compliance with state and federal regulations.
  • To assist in the investigation of incidents to gathering information on root cause in order to ensure safety and compliance with state and federal procedures and ensure deficiencies are corrected to prevent recurrence.
  • To compose reports such as field evaluations, construction inspections, natural gas incident documentation, and follow-up notices in order to report findings and document compliance with state and federal guidelines.
  • To compose official letters such as Notices of Violation in order to notify operators of violations that will result in compliance by the operator.
  • To cooperate with federal monitoring of the state program to assure program compliance with certification requirements.
  • To attend pipeline safety training courses conducted by PHMSA’s office of Training and Qualifications (TQ) and others as directed or required.
  • To assist in the coordination and enforcement of Dig-Safe laws and federal pipeline safety enforcement through an agreement with the U.S. Department of Transportation, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) under Pipeline Safety Code of Federal Regulations CFR- Chapter 49 Parts §190-§199 and Part §40, inclusive (or any applicable successor provisions).
  • To perform annual record and field operator audits and provide written documentation of all findings including areas in violation, areas of concern, and improvement opportunities.
  • To ensure all activities, contacts, and meetings are properly documented and documentation is appropriately electronically filed.
  • To coordinate utility operations data to include outage reports from all regulated utilities as a key partner in ESF-12 (energy) and work at the Emergency Management Agency’s Emergency Operations Center (EOC) during inclement weather and other times of activation as deemed necessary by a supervisor.
  • To be on call and to respond to emergency situations as needed.
  • To investigate consumer complaints regarding gas utility services or lack of service.
  • To do related work as required.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS FOR APPOINTMENT:

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND CAPACITIES: A working knowledge and understanding of engineering principles, theories and processes; knowledge of the fundamental principles and practices of engineering in natural gas and the ability to apply such knowledge to relevant engineering problems encountered in the construction, maintenance, repair, and operation of a gas utility; knowledge of inspection and research techniques involved in the review of gas operators' records; the ability to conduct audits and inspections of gas pipelines; familiarity with the Pipeline Safety Regulations – 49 CFR Parts 190 through 199 and Part 40 (or any applicable successor provision); familiarity with Rhode Island’s One-Call regulations regarding underground utility location and damage prevention; the ability to apply engineering concepts in conducting pipeline safety inspections; the ability to interpret and understand regulations and standards; the ability to develop schedules to ensure that required inspections and follow-up inspections are completed; the ability to prepare supporting material and justification for grant and budget requests; the ability to establish and maintain an effective working relationships with superiors, subordinates, public utility personnel, and the public; and related capacities and abilities.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

Education: Possession of a Bachelor of Science degree from a college of recognized standing in Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or a closely related field; and

Experience: A minimum of one (1) year of employment in a technical position in a Utility engineering program or other comparable level at a public agency or in a private industry.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS:

1. Within three (3) years of appointment, must successfully complete the Federal Department of Transportation, Pipeline & Hazardous Materials Safety Administration’s Basic Gas Inspector Training Program.

2. As a condition of employment, must remain current with all training and certifications as outlined by PHMSA.

3. Must complete specialized elective training and other training(s) as directed by the agency.

Supplemental Information

GENERAL STATEMENT OF DUTIES: To assist with inspections of natural gas pipeline facilities (such as standard, construction, and follow-up inspections) including inspecting and observing critical valves, regulator stations, master meters, relief valves, pressure recorders, odorizers, and rectifiers using Field Evaluation forms; to utilize specialized equipment such as multi-meters and odorometers; to follow applicable guidelines and regulations, supervisory directives, and professional standards in order to determine compliance with state and federal regulations regarding design, installation, operation, and maintenance of facilities; and to do related work as required. description:
Why MSI? We thrive on solving challenges.

The Internal Controls Associate is responsible for supporting and enhancing the organization's overall internal control environment across business operations, technology platforms, financial reporting, information security, regulatory compliance, and risk management activities. This role evaluates the design and effectiveness of controls, documents key processes and procedures, maintains evidence to demonstrate control performance, and collaborates with business and technology teams to identify, assess, and mitigate risks.

The Internal Controls Associate assists with internal audits, operational reviews, control testing and/or execution, remediation efforts, and compliance initiatives related to applicable laws, regulations, industry standards, and contractual obligations. Responsibilities extend beyond any single regulatory framework and may include supporting compliance with Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX), privacy regulations, cybersecurity requirements, insurance industry regulations, and other governance, risk, and compliance obligations as applicable to the organization.

This position plays a key role in promoting a strong control culture by continuously assessing organizational risks, identifying control gaps, recommending improvements, and helping ensure that the company's overall control environment remains effective, sustainable, and aligned with business objectives, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.

Key Responsibilities

Internal Control Program Administration

  • Assist in the design, implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the organization's internal control framework.
  • Document and maintain policies, procedures, process flows, risk and control matrices (RCMs), and control narratives in alignment with COSO principles.
  • Ensure controls are appropriately designed to mitigate identified business, operational, financial, compliance, and technology risks.

Risk Assessment and Control Design

  • Perform periodic risk assessments across business and technology functions.
  • Identify control gaps, emerging risks, and process inefficiencies.
  • Develop and recommend risk mitigation strategies and control enhancements.
  • Support enterprise risk management and compliance initiatives.

Control Testing and Monitoring

  • Develop and execute control testing procedures to evaluate control design and operating effectiveness.
  • Analyze testing results, identify deficiencies, and track remediation activities.
  • Maintain evidence supporting control execution and effectiveness.
  • Monitor key controls through continuous auditing and data analytics techniques where applicable.

Regulatory and Compliance Support

  • Support compliance with applicable regulations, standards, and contractual obligations, including:
    • Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX)
    • State insurance regulations
    • Privacy regulations (CCPA, CPRA, GDPR, etc.)
    • Cybersecurity and information security requirements
    • SOC reporting, PCI DSS, and other industry-specific frameworks as applicable
  • Assist in preparing regulatory examinations, audits, and compliance assessments.

Audit Coordination and Management

  • Serve as a primary liaison for Internal Audit and external auditors.
  • Coordinate audit requests and facilitate walkthroughs, interviews, and evidence collection.
  • Respond to audit inquiries and support remediation efforts.
  • Track audit findings and ensure corrective actions are implemented timely.

Operational and Business Process Reviews

  • Evaluate operational processes to identify risks, inefficiencies, and control weaknesses.
  • Conduct special reviews and investigations relating to control failures, incidents, or identified concerns.
  • Participate in assessments related to fraud prevention, business continuity, vendor management, and cybersecurity.

Reporting and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Prepare clear, concise, and audit-ready reports summarizing risks, control effectiveness, and recommendations.
  • Communicate findings and corrective action plans to business and technology leadership.
  • Escalate significant issues and emerging risks appropriately.
  • Present control-related information to management committees and stakeholders.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to enhance operational efficiency, governance, and compliance processes.
  • Assist in developing metrics, dashboards, and reporting to monitor control effectiveness.
  • Promote a culture of accountability, risk awareness, and strong internal controls throughout the organization.
  • Stay informed on regulatory changes, emerging risks, and industry best practices affecting the insurance sector.

Other Duties

  • Support control, audit, risk management, governance, compliance, and operational initiatives as assigned by Internal Controls leadership.
  • Perform additional control-related activities necessary to maintain an effective enterprise-wide control environment.

Core Competencies that predict success in a high-accountability Internal Controls Role:

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance or Tech preferred
  • 1-2 years of experience in internal controls, external or internal audit positions.
  • Big four or banking experience is a plus.
  • Demonstrated ability to consistently deliver on commitments and manage competing priorities.
  • Strong organizational, planning, and project management skills.
  • Sound professional judgment and risk-based decision-making capabilities.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and analytical thinking.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Demonstrated accountability, ownership, and follow-through.
  • Strong listening skills and openness to coaching and feedback.
  • Ability to quickly learn new systems, regulations, and business processes.
  • Proven ability to build effective working relationships and influence stakeholders.
  • Must demonstrate the organization’s core values, exuding behavior aligned with the firm’s culture.

Special Working Conditions:

Fast-paced, multi-tasking and agile environment.

Must be able to interact effectively with various levels of management both inside and outside the organization.

Important Notice:

This position description is intended to describe the level of work required of the person performing in the role and is not a contract. The essential responsibilities are outlined; other duties may be assigned as needs arise or as required to support the Firm.

title: Bilingual Systems Quality Analyst II (100% Remote)
description:
TELUS Health is empowering every person to live their healthiest life. Guided by our vision, we are leveraging the power of our leading edge technology and focusing on the uniqueness of each individual to create the future of health. As a global-leading health and well-being provider – encompassing physical, mental and financial health – TELUS Health is improving health outcomes for consumers, patients, healthcare professionals, employers and employees.

As a Bilingual Quality Assurance Analyst at TELUS Health, you'll spend your days ensuring the quality and reliability of our health technology solutions within an Agile development environment. You'll analyze technical documents, design comprehensive test strategies, execute testing procedures, and collaborate with cross-functional teams including Functional Leads, Business Analysts, Solution Designers, and Developers to identify and resolve issues.

Working in a bilingual environment, you'll contribute to the full software testing lifecycle while mentoring junior team members and supporting the delivery of critical applications that thousands of users across North America rely on.

What You'll Do

  • Communicate with Functional Leads, Business Analysts, Solution Designers, and Developers to gain clear understanding of testing scope
  • Analyze technical documents to identify high-level test scenarios and develop comprehensive test cases
  • Apply structured testing techniques to create positive and negative test cases with expected results and test data
  • Maintain and update test suites based on new or changed functionalities
  • Prioritize and execute manual test scripts with precision and attention to detail
  • Report defects, follow up on resolution within established timeframes, and perform retesting
  • Work closely with QA Leads to report testing progress and raise flags on potential risks to deadlines or quality
  • Support and peer-review tasks of other QA resources, particularly those with less experience
  • Provide client support and training when required
  • Deliver all QA-related tasks according to defined standards and procedures in a timely manner
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams in Agile ceremonies on stable, long-term projects that impact healthcare technology

What You Bring

Required:

  • Bilingual proficiency (English and French) - excellent written and oral communication skills
  • University degree in computer science, mathematics, or related discipline
  • Minimum 2 years of relevant Quality Assurance experience
  • Detail-oriented mindset with strong analytical skills
  • Ability to put yourself in clients' shoes and understand external customer requirements from a testing perspective
  • Curious, disciplined, and creative approach to problem-solving
  • Ability to use concepts and data to approach problems in a structured manner
  • Clear and constructive communication skills with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Ability to think from users' perspective
  • Commitment to learning and professional growth
  • Ability to work effectively in a remote/hybrid environment
  • Availability to travel within Canada

Assets:

  • Experience in pension plan administration or financial services industry
  • Experience using Azure DevOps (ADO) for test management and defect tracking
  • Experience with Selenium and Java

What's In It For You

  • 100% remote work flexibility with optional office access (hybrid mode available)
  • Full TELUS Health benefits package including pension plan with employer contribution
  • Paid vacation and wellness days
  • Performance bonus opportunities
  • Excellent leadership and mentorship opportunities
  • Collaborative team environment that values your contributions
  • Professional development in Canada's leading health technology company
  • Flexible schedule supporting work-life balance

Actual total compensation will be determined based on factors such as knowledge, skills, performance and experience. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply, even if the posted salary range doesn't match your expectations. We're open to discussing competitive compensation packages tailored to your experience level and expertise.

TELUS Health offers rewarding benefits, which may vary per job function, such as:
Comprehensive total rewards package highlighting competitive salary and bonus structures, minimum 3 weeks of vacation, and flexible benefits plan to meet the needs of you and your family
Flexibility to work in-office, virtually or a combination of both
Generous company matched pension
Opportunity to give back to communities in which we work, live and serve
Career growth and learning & development opportunities to develop your skills
And much more…

Intermediate knowledge of English is required because you will most of the time interact in English with external parties (clients, suppliers, candidates, external partners, etc.); interact in English with internal parties (colleagues, internal partners, stakeholders, etc.); and work with IT tools whose interface is only accessible in English as part of this position's main responsibilities given its international scope.

A bit about us

We’re a people-focused, customer-first, purpose-driven team who works together every day to innovate and do good. We improve lives through our technology solutions and foster a culture of innovation that empowers team members to solve complex problems and create remarkable human outcomes in a digital world.

TELUS is proud to foster an inclusive culture that embraces diversity. We are committed to fair employment practices and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment. We offer accommodation for applicants with disabilities, as required, during the recruitment process.

description:
Job Location:

Desert Islands Resort & Spa by Anantara



Anantara Hotels & Resorts is a global luxury hotel and resort brand rooted in Thai culture, with an intrinsic sense of authentic hospitality. Inspired by the Sanskrit word meaning ‘without end’, our spirit embodies freedom, movement, and harmony. We believe every journey should leave a lasting impression — for our guests and for our people.


Founded in 2001 in Thailand, we have since expanded across the world, welcoming guests in some of the world’s most captivating locales — from pristine beaches and private islands to ancient sites and vibrant metropolises. If you are driven by a passion for generosity, warmth and heartfelt hospitality, Anantara offers a career without limits.


Job Summary

The Painter is responsible for maintaining the hotel’s interior and exterior appearance by carrying out painting, touch-up, surface preparation, and related maintenance works. The role ensures all areas are maintained to the hotel’s quality, safety, and aesthetic standards while minimizing disruption to guests and hotel operations.

Key Responsibilities

title: Portfolio Management Professional, Project Finance
description:
Looking for a role where you can safeguard and steer a growing portfolio of non-recourse financings after financial close? Join our Project and Asset Finance team in Copenhagen as a Portfolio Management Professional and help manage EE's financing obligations across Europe.

European Energy is a growing company in the renewable energy sector. We are a privately owned Danish company founded in 2004, with our headquarters in Copenhagen. We develop, construct, finance, and operate solar (PV) and wind energy projects globally, as well as Power-to-X projects. In addition, we explore new technologies, including battery storage, biogas, and carbon capture. Our core values form the foundation of everything we do: In It Together, Trust and Courage, Ambition, Excitement, Inclusion, and Agility.

Your New Team

As a part of the CCO Area, the Project and Asset Finance team is responsible for sourcing all financing needed to construct EE's project pipeline, and for managing that financing through construction and operation.

In this role, you will work directly with the Global Head of Project and Asset Finance, the transaction deal teams, Asset Management, and Treasury, as well as the more than 25 other members of the broader M&A and Project Finance department dedicated to commercialising EE's asset portfolio.

Your New Role

As our new Portfolio Management Professional, you will, in collaboration with colleagues within our Asset Management and Treasury departments, take ownership of EE's financing obligations once a transaction reaches financial close. You will track asset finance transactions through construction and operation, quality-assure disbursements, reporting, waivers, and amendments, and act as the link between the deal team, Asset Management, and Treasury. This is a role for someone who wants broad visibility across a growing portfolio of non-recourse financings and a direct hand in keeping it in good order.

Your Responsibilities

  • Assist with transaction closing and documentation ahead of financial close.

  • Ensure a timely, clear, and detailed handoff of post-closing responsibilities to other internal stakeholders.

  • Shadow and track all transactions throughout construction, providing support and quality assurance on disbursements, construction reporting, waivers, and amendments.

  • Support and quality-assure the work of Asset Management during material restructurings

  • and amendments.

  • Quality-assure the payment of scheduled principal and interest to lenders.

  • Track all asset finance transactions booked across the portfolio.

  • Coordinate with Treasury to provide timely and accurate information on portfolio exposures.

  • Manage all relationships with lender portfolio management counterparties.

  • Support in periodic and ah-hoc reporting of portfolio obligations and status.

  • Collaborate with M&A colleagues on common reporting obligations.

Prerequisites to progress in the job

  • You have a minimum of 4 years of relevant experience in project finance, loan or portfolio administration, agency, or credit/portfolio monitoring roles, ideally within renewable energy or infrastructure.

  • You have experience with post-closing management of non-recourse financings, including disbursements, covenant compliance, and reporting obligations.

  • You have exposure to restructurings, workouts, or amendments, and are comfortable in quality-assuring the work of others.

  • You have strong attention to detail and can work confidently across a large, growing portfolio of transactions.

  • You have solid financial modelling and analytical skills, and a robust understanding of financing documentation.

As a person, you are structured and detail-oriented and can be trusted to keep track of many transactions in parallel without losing sight of what matters. You are a natural coordinator, comfortable working across the deal team, Asset Management, and Treasury, and you communicate clearly with both technical and financial audiences. You have a genuine interest in the financial market and the renewable energy sector.

You may be asked to travel occasionally to meet with stakeholders across Europe.

With us you get

  • Close collaboration with senior colleagues and meaningful deal ownership from day one

  • A culture of knowledge sharing and international collaboration across 21+ countries

  • Flexible work policy and a diverse, inclusive work environment

  • Opportunities for career advancement in a growing company and sector

  • Six weeks of paid annual leave, a subsidised lunch scheme, employee discounts on glasses, furniture, and massage, free access to a gym, a mobile phone for both professional and personal use, and access to professional development opportunities, including on-the-job learning, internal and external training, and networking.

European Energy at a glance — The Power of Tomorrow, Today

We are now more than 970 employees with 51 nationalities represented in 21 countries, and we are growing rapidly in both Copenhagen and across our global offices. We all work for our common goal: to be a leading partner in the renewable energy transition and to create The Power of Tomorrow, Today.

Our working environment is built on mutual respect for the varied strengths and talents of our employees, with a flat hierarchy and a culture that encourages initiative and innovation. Our employees value our flexible working culture, which supports a better balance between work and personal life. We are a team, whether it is in the workplace, on our company trips, or during our weekly company training sessions. At European Energy, you will work with colleagues from around the world and become part of a collaborative international network.

We lead with purpose

At European Energy, our leadership culture is built on six guiding principles that shape how we collaborate, make decisions, and grow together. These principles help us act responsibly and empower each other to succeed.

Apply now

Workplace: Søborg, Denmark

Reference: Jeremy Bennett, Director, Global Head of Project and Asset Finance

To support a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly ask that you do not include a photograph in your CV. We assess all candidates based on their skills, experience, qualifications, and potential to succeed in the role. We review applications and conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and will close the position once a suitable candidate has been identified. We therefore encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we do not accept applications via email or any other direct messaging channels. Applications must be submitted through the designated application link.

Background check: As a last step of the hiring process, a background check will be conducted on the final candidate. This is to safeguard our operations and ensure compliance with EU regulations for critical infrastructure. The check can include verification of identity, employment history, and criminal records.

title: HR Lead Affiliates
description:
HR Lead for Affiliates Fiducre & Record Credits

Orange Contract | HR | Experienced | Belgium | Brussels | 19 | HRBP V

Your work environment

About Fiducre

Fiducre is a leading player in the area of debt recovery in Belgium. The company is a subsidiary of ING Belgium and employs around 160 people. The clients are Belgian financial institutions and banks.

The company has two main activities:

Fiducre is active on the Belgian debt recovery market, purchasing recent or depreciated portfolios from the mother company (ING Belgium) and from Record Credits (subsidiary of ING Belgium) and also from other financial institutions. The recovery and risk of default is supported by Fiducre since it recovers the outstanding debts for own account. ING Belgium and Record Credits also outsource their arrears management to Fiducre. For these activities Fiducre is mandated by ING Belgium and Record Credits.

About Record Credits

Record Credits is the market leader in the Belgian credit brokerage market and focuses on private individuals. It works with an extensive network of independent credit brokers and garages and offers its customers a full range of home and consumer loans. It is a subsidiary of ING Belgium and employs over 100 people.

Your role

This role reports hierarchically to the HR Lead for Retail Banking and functionally to both the CEO of Fiducre and the CEO of Record Credits. You lead the team of 4 HR employees and 1 communication officer. Your place of employment is Brussels (Marnix), but you also make regular trips to Ghent (where a part of the Fiducre employees is stationedirectly to the HR Director of ING Belgium.

As Head of People & Culture you co-create the Human Resources strategy for both Fiducre and Record Credits. You are responsible for HR "end to end" and lead the joint HR department of both companies. You

work with the business leadership teams to shape and implement the people agenda within the business through enhancing leadership capabilities and driving strategic people decisions, such as organizational effectiveness, talent and succession planning, people development and team performance.

As people management, corporate culture and communication have a lot of common ground, you will also manage the communication strategy within Fiducre and work on cultural and wellbeing initiatives in general.

Your key responsibilities

You are responsible for building a strong relationship within the business leadership teams of both companies and will bring in-depth specialist knowledge in multiple HR areas of expertise. Equally, you bring in a strong business acumen and affinity with the banking business.

“End to end” HR management

  • You manage all HR aspects within the company, hiring to firing” (the majority of the HR processes being different to the processes on ING level).
  • You organise and coordinate the HR administrative processes like payroll, time & absence, benefits…). You ensure competitive and compliant reward structures and organize and coordinate the yearly remuneration reviews.
  • You oversee and organize recruitment processes to attract and retain talent, you focus on workforce planning, talent management and career guidance.
  • You maintain and coordinate, together with the CEO, the relations with the social partners (Works Council, Committee for Prevention, Trade Union delegation). You are responsible for the drafting and implementation of the companies’ CLA’s.
  • HR Policies, Compliance & Risk: You manage and draft policies, procedures, and ensure adherence to labour laws and regulations. You monitor the Compliance and Risk aspects within the HR domain.
  • You manage the contractual relations of HR with external partners and suppliers, including with the Social Secretariat.

Communication

You lead the communication officer responsible for all external and internal communications. Together with the communication officer, you take on an advisory role to various departments regarding communication in the broadest sense of the word and you monitor the house style and the right "tone-of-voice" in our communications. You develop a solid internal and external employer branding strategy.

Culture, wellbeing and prevention

You actively support the management team in the renewal of the company culture by promoting the values of the company, working on employer branding and driving initiatives that promote a positive, inclusive, and high-performance culture. You proactively work on different wellbeing initiatives and in collaboration with the prevention advisors, you make sure all regulation on prevention are proactively followed up. You are the Chairman of the Prevention Committee.

How to succeed?

In summary, the areas where you make impact are as follows:

  • Shaping the People and Business Agenda and drive Change - partner with the management teams to ensure that the right core people capabilities are available to allow for current and future business success.
  • Building a Performance Culture – coach leaders in using performance and talent management solutions to drive individual and team performance.
  • Promoting and apply as much as possible global people solutions that meet business needs - bring and apply global people solutions, developed by the Community of Expertise, to the specific business context.

What do you bring to the team ?

  • Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.
  • Affinity with numbers and data and a good understanding on how data analysis and reporting support building the people agenda.
  • Demonstrated consultation skills to help the business in understanding their people needs and propose the right solution to fit that need.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with a clear demonstration of influencing business leaders.
  • Strong business acumen and ability to adapt quickly to financial industry, a good understanding of financial sector is a plus.

You are a strong communicator at all levels of the organization, with story-telling abilities. Fluent in English (speaking and writing) and good knowledge of French and/or Dutch. You have a Master’s degree level working/thinking capacity and 8–10 years of HR experience, including leadership roles.

We offer you

A clear purpose, a unique offer and a range of flexible compensation and other benefits:

  • personal growth & challenging work with opportunities to realise your ambitions
  • you can count on a range of opportunities to invest in your personal and professional growth.

title: Supplier Quality Senior Specialist
description:

  • Strong familiarity with Chinese and international codes (e.g., GB/T 150, NB/T 47003.1/2, SH/T 3513, ASME B16.5). Knowledge of Chinese TSG pressure vessel regulations is an advantage.

title: Project Manager
description:
Role: Project Manager

Location: Kista (Stockholm), Sweden

Contract type: full-time, permanent role

About Marioff

For four decades, Marioff has been driven by the challenge of keeping people and businesses safe. Today, we are the global leader in high-pressure water mist fire protection with our HI-FOG system, setting new standards and pushing the fire protection industry forward. Rooted in Nordic innovation and delivering globally, Marioff is home to those who approach challenges with an innovative mindset, persistence, and an unwavering commitment to quality. We believe that delivering peace of mind and reliability to our customers requires empowering diverse teams to collaborate towards common success, creating a lasting impact.


At Marioff, more than 500 motivated professionals work across the globe. As a truly global company, we value the diversity of roles and skills within our team, with colleagues from nearly 30 nationalities collaborating towards a common goal.


With our head office in Vantaa and our factory in Kerava, Finland, we have a global reach with subsidiaries in France, Germany, Italy, North America, Spain, Sweden, Poland, the United Kingdom, and China.

About the role

At Marioff Sweden our mission is to deliver cutting-edge HI-FOG high-pressure water mist fire suppression systems to our esteemed customers. We are searching for a dynamic and dedicated Project Manager to join our professional organization.

Requirements

To be successful in this role, you must have:


  • Minimum 5 years of professional experience in a relevant role / area of responsibility, preferably from the construction/building services engineering industry
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in a related technical field (Mechanical, Building Services Engineering, HVAC, Hydraulics, Electrical or Fire Protection), or acquired equivalent competence through other means that we consider comparable
  • Excellent communication skills with a strong fluency in Swedish and English language
  • Great knowledge of project management, exceptional organizational skills, multitasking ability and attention to detail
  • Experience with budget management and commercial skills, contract creation
  • Willingness to travel, Category B driver's license
  • Strong computer skills & MS Office knowledge
  • Leadership and people management skills, ability to work effectively in a team environment and independently as well
  • Quality-and customer focused mindset
  • Ability to work in a structured and methodical way

Although not necessary, it would be an advantage:

  • Experience from the following fields: Fire Suppression /HVAC/Gas systems/Sanitary products/Wastewater treatment or other building services/construction engineering field
  • Knowledge of fire protection standards and regulations
  • Experience working with standards, regulations, and technical guidelines related to fire protection is a plus. You do not need to be an expert in specific standards, but a general understanding of how such frameworks are applied in engineering projects would be beneficial.
  • Personal certification in the fire protection (SBSC or RISE) area is considered an advantage.
  • Experience/knowledge with the Autodesk suite including Autodesk Forma


Responsibilities

As a Project Manager, you will be entrusted with the critical task of overseeing the high-quality delivery of HI-FOG water mist fire suppression system projects to our customers. Your mission: to ensure that our customers' needs, specifications and requirements are not only met, all while upholding the critical standards of security and precision.


  • Project planning & scheduling
  • Verification of system/plant design parameters
  • Construction monitoring & review of construction site documents
  • Proactive management of project execution phase, including installation & commissioning oversight
  • Subcontractor and supplier management through the project lifecycle
  • Project controlling & performance monitoring, cost control throughout the entire project duration
  • Customer & stakeholder management, coordination of the project team
  • Creation of project documentation and review of audit documents
  • Quality assurance certification support
  • Project forecasting, preparation of offers and all necessary documents for project accounting

Benefits

We are committed to offering competitive benefits programs for all of our employees, and enhancing our programs when necessary.

  • Competitive compensation
  • Bonus system
  • Professional development opportunities
  • An influential role in a professional organization

Our commitment to you

We offer you a dynamic and international work environment in a company with high technology products, a strong growth strategy and people who are passionate about fire safety. At Marioff we value diversity in all its forms and we believe that it is our excellent, highly skilled people who make success, competitive excellence and innovation happen. Join us to our mission to protect people, property and business continuity!

title: Supervisor Mill Operations
description:
WHAT WE OFFER

Your journey with Capstone Copper starts here. At Capstone, our people are the heart of our organization. We are focused on growth and are committed to unlocking the full potential of ourselves, our teams and our resources. We invest in our people to develop a skilled and engaged workforce, not only for today, but for the future. If you are looking for a purposeful, performance-driven and dynamic work environment, join us!


Pinto Valley is an open-pit copper mine located at the west end of the historic Globe-Miami mining district of central Arizona, approximately 80 miles east of Phoenix. Pinto Valley has been in operation since 1972 and has produced more than four billion pounds of copper. Acquired by Capstone from BHP in 2013, the mine is fully permitted through 2039 and a study is underway to potentially extend the mine life through 2050.


Our proximity to the Greater Phoenix metro area provides prospective employees with the option to live in communities such as Mesa, Apache Junction, Gilbert, Chandler, San Tan Valley, or Florence. Our location offers a unique work-life balance, blending the rewarding opportunities of the mining industry with easy access to the vibrant energy of Downtown Phoenix, making it an ideal choice for both individuals and their families.


Capstone employees are eligible for an extensive total rewards package, designed to support your physical, mental, financial, and emotional well-being. This package includes, but is not limited to:

  • 401(k) Savings Plan – Eligible from day one, contribute up to 90% of your salary with a dollar-for-dollar company match up to 6%, fully vested immediately.
  • Retirement Boost – The company contributes 8.5% of your salary, with 100% immediate vesting.
  • Employee Share Purchase Plan – After three months, contribute 2% to 7% of your salary (max $5,000/year) to buy company shares, with a 50% company match, fully vested upon grant.
  • Annual Short Term Incentive Bonus – Up to 15%
  • We offer a 7-on, 7-off schedule that consists of one week of 12-hour day shifts followed by one week off, followed by one week of 12-hour night shifts. These schedules offer a great work-life balance with ample time for rest and personal activities.
  • Affordable Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits (effective on start date), including Telehealth options and additional supplemental insurances
  • Disability and Life Insurance (effective on start date)
  • Paid time-off, including vacation, holidays, sick leave, and parental leave
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Internal progression opportunities
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Discounted insurance plans for pets, automobiles and homes



POSITION OVERVIEW
The Supervisor, Mill Operations is responsible for directing and supervising processing activities to safely and effectively process ore while achieving HSEC, production, concentrate grade, quality, and cost targets. The role oversees day-to-day mill operations, resource allocation, staffing, production execution, and coordination with maintenance and other processing functions.
This position provides operational leadership to Processing Production Technicians, ensures compliance with company and MSHA requirements, and coordinates short- and long-term production and maintenance activities. The Supervisor also monitors operational performance, addresses issues in real time, maintains accurate shift reporting, and supports continuous improvement across assigned processing circuits.


POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES
• Safety & Compliance: Ensure employees and contractors work in compliance with Pinto Valley Mine, MSHA, company safety requirements, standard operating procedures, and applicable local, state, and federal regulations.
• Training & Certification: Ensure employees and contractors are properly trained and certified for assigned tasks. Coordinate with the Processing Training Coordinator to address current and future training needs.
• Team Leadership: Build and maintain an effective operations team through recruitment, development, coaching, performance feedback, and performance reviews.
• Employee Development: Establish clear learning objectives and work with team members to support professional development and operational competency.
• Labor & Resource Planning: Ensure appropriate manpower, equipment, and resources are available to meet planned production activities while maintaining budgeted costs.
• Production Execution: Direct mill operations to achieve production, concentrate grade, quality, HSEC, and cost targets. Identify and correct operational issues as they arise.
• Work Planning: Establish clear work plans, priorities, and expectations to support department and production objectives.
• Operational Coordination: Coordinate with Processing Maintenance, Electrical and Instrumentation, Tailings, Metallurgy, Mine Operations, and other departments to support safe and reliable production.
• Maintenance Coordination: Ensure equipment is operated using proper practices and coordinate maintenance activities to maintain equipment availability and reliability.
• Maintenance Planning: Review and coordinate short- and long-term maintenance plans and schedules with production requirements, including Down Day planning and scheduling.
• SAP & Work Notifications: Enter maintenance work notifications in SAP and maintain communication between operators and maintenance personnel regarding reported equipment issues.
• Operational Reporting: Ensure accurate operational data is captured and complete required daily, shift, weekly, and monthly reporting.
• Shift Documentation: Complete short-interval control reports, shift handovers, 24-hour reports, downtime entries, and other required operational documentation.
• Process Optimization: Identify opportunities to improve production practices, operating processes, equipment performance, and overall department efficiency.
• Continuous Improvement: Implement initiatives, programs, processes, and practices that improve operational performance and support organizational requirements.
• Issue Resolution: Identify potential operational issues and work with Mine and Processing management to prevent, mitigate, and resolve problems in real time.
• Budget Support: Provide input to Mill Operations leadership regarding department budget development and resource requirements.
• Governance & Standards: Implement operational programs, processes, and policies in accordance with company governance requirements and applicable standards.
• Operational Leadership: Provide technical expertise, leadership, and guidance to internal and external departments as required.
• Assigned Processing Areas: Depending on operational needs, responsibilities may include primary and fine crushing, grinding and tail thickener circuits, copper/moly flotation, and filter plant operations.
• Company Values: Demonstrate accountability, operational excellence, care for employees, and a commitment to safety in all activities.
• Other Duties: Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned or required.


POSITION REQUIREMENTS
Required
• Three years of concentrator/mill-related experience in production execution areas.
• Strong working knowledge of processing operations, including applicable theories, practices, methods, and procedures.
• Ability to operate and make decisions in a production environment while maintaining safety, quality, and production requirements.
• Ability to effectively coordinate personnel, equipment, maintenance activities, and production priorities.
• Ability to speak, comprehend, read, and write English.

Preferred
• Associate’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
• SAP experience.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Outlook.
WORK ENVIRONMENT / PHYSICAL DEMANDS
• Work is performed in mine, concentrator, and tailings areas.
• Approximately 25% office environment and 75% field environment.
• Ability to stand and walk for short durations, including walking up and down stairs and across uneven surfaces.
• Regular exposure to active mining and processing operations and associated industrial conditions.
• Ability to work in field environments while monitoring equipment, production activities, and employee performance.


All candidates will be required to complete a pre-employment medical exam, drug and alcohol test, and background check. All positions require a pre-placement physical examination to ensure candidates are 'fit for duty’. Additional training and/or testing may be required. Capstone maintains a drug and alcohol-free workplace.

Banana Island Resort Doha By Anantara

The role requires a versatile technician with practical knowledge across multiple maintenance disciplines, including electrical, plumbing, HVAC, carpentry, painting, and general building maintenance.

  • Ability to use common maintenance tools and equipment safely.
  • Good understanding of health and safety procedures.

Key Competencies

  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Good technical and practical skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Good communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and respond effectively to urgent maintenance requests.
  • Attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Flexible and willing to work shifts, weekends, and public holidays when required.
  • Physically fit and able to perform hands-on maintenance work.
  • Positive attitude and service-oriented approach.

title: Importing Coordinator
description:
Position Summary

Austin Hose is seeking an organized, detail-oriented Import Coordinator to manage and coordinate imported shipments from initial shipment notification through final receiving and closeout.

This position serves as the primary point of coordination between Purchasing, freight forwarders, vendors, receiving branches, and Accounting. The Import Coordinator is responsible for keeping shipments on track, maintaining accurate documentation, coordinating deliveries, supporting landed-cost calculations, reconciling receiving information, and ensuring each import is properly completed and closed.

Key Responsibilities

  • Monitor and track incoming import shipments, estimated arrival dates, commercial invoices, packing lists, and related documentation.
  • Maintain accurate shipment, purchase order, container, delivery, and cost information within company systems.
  • Coordinate delivery appointments with freight forwarders and receiving locations.
  • Communicate shipment schedules, changes, delays, and delivery information to appropriate teams.
  • Review receiving discrepancies and coordinate resolution with Purchasing leadership.
  • Collect freight, tariff/duty, packing, and other import-related costs.
  • Calculate and allocate landed costs using established company processes.
  • Update purchase order costs and coordinate release of shipments for receiving.
  • Reconcile received quantities and costs against shipment documentation.
  • Maintain complete supporting documentation and an accurate audit trail for each shipment.
  • Coordinate shipment closeout once receiving, costs, documentation, and required system updates are complete.
  • Assist with vendor credits, product returns, and import-related inventory issues.
  • Follow up on missing information and proactively keep shipments and outstanding issues moving toward resolution.
  • Maintain organized records so open shipments can be easily understood and continued by another trained team member when needed.

title: Senior Product Manager - Digital Investment Products
description:
Senior Product Manager - Digital Investments

Amsterdam | 36–40 hours

Shape the next generation of digital investment propositions for our customers. As Senior Product Manager, you will turn customer and market insights into compelling products, build support for a clear vision and lead complex initiatives from first concept to successful rollout.

The team
The Digital Investments Product Management team identifies unmet customer needs and market opportunities and turns them into distinctive, sustainable investment propositions. We are responsible for Self Invest (Brokerage), Easy Invest and Pension Investing in the Netherlands. Together with our colleagues from Marketing, Risk, and IT, we create an excellent digital platform experience while safeguarding customer interests, regulatory requirements and profitability.

You will join a collaborative, ambitious environment in which evidence, clear choices and stakeholder alignment matter. Your work will range from improving today’s customer journeys to defining propositions and capabilities that will shape our investment offering for years to come.

Roles and responsibilities
You will lead proposition development and continuous improvement across our digital investment products, translating strategic opportunities into customer value and measurable business results.

  • Leading proposition initiatives from opportunity identification and solution definition through development, launch and optimisation.
  • Developing a clear product vision, roadmap and value story, and securing commitment from teams and senior stakeholders.
  • Turning market, customer and performance insights into evidence-based priorities, requirements and business cases.
  • Defining customer journeys and business requirements in close collaboration with customer experience specialists, engineers and other delivery partners.
  • Testing the delivered key features of IT teams to ensure they meet the business and customer requirements.

What could it look like specifically?

  • Creating a pension plan conversation that helps customers and advisers understand pension needs, including pricing, tooling and rollout strategy.
  • Developing a pension payout product from early solution definition and refinement through delivery and market rollout.
  • Adding parental controls to our investment products as part of a Child Investing proposition to meet key customer needs.
  • Identifying and refining the key platform features needed to make ING the home of the best-in-class Brokerage platform.
  • Optimising existing investment features and flows using customer feedback and continuous analysis to reduce friction and improve outcomes.
  • Collaborating with other ING countries and the Global Platform team to shape the future vision for investment products and represent the needs of customers in the Netherlands.


How to succeed
We hire smart people like you for your potential. Our biggest expectation is that you’ll stay curious. Keep learning. Take on responsibility. In return, we’ll back you to develop into an even more awesome version of yourself.

To be successful in this role, you bring:

  • A proven ability to lead complex, long-term product or proposition programmes involving multiple teams, dependencies and stakeholders.
  • Strong proposition development and lifecycle management skills, from customer problem and market opportunity to launch and optimisation.
  • Customer experience expertise and the ability to translate research and journey insights into intuitive digital solutions.
  • Experience bridging business and technology, including defining clear, actionable requirements with engineering and platform teams.
  • Persuasive communication skills: you make the product vision and customer need tangible and create buy-in across a broad stakeholder landscape.
  • Strong analytical and commercial judgement, with the ability to support recommendations through customer data, market analysis and robust business cases.
  • Solid knowledge of pension investing and/or brokerage is strongly preferred.

Rewards and benefits
We want to make sure that it’s possible for you to strike the right balance between your career and your private life. Find out more about our employment conditions.


The benefits of working with us at ING include:

  • 25-28 vacation days depending on contract
  • Pension scheme
  • 13th month salary
  • 8% Holiday payment
  • Hybrid working
  • Personal growth and challenging work with endless possibilities
  • An informal working environment with innovative colleagues

Discover what we do and what we can offer you.

description:
Within our department IT Front & Package with the mission of developing and maintaining our web applications and all our third-party applications, we are seeking a Web Analyst Developer. With your full-stack developer background, you will be responsible for handling both the front-end and back-end aspects of web applications and will work closely with our external teams to deliver high-quality software solutions. As analyst you will be responsible to transpose requirements into solutions.

The team consists of 8 colleagues who are waiting just for you!

Your responsibilities

As Web Analyst Developer your responsibilities will include:

  • Full-Stack Development: Design, develop, and maintain web applications using Angular for the front-end and .NET for the back-end.

  • As Third line support, you will participate in production incident trouble shooting.

  • Analyse business and technical requirements to develop robust, scalable, and secure solutions.

  • Front-End Development: Implement responsive and user-friendly UI designs using Angular/Agular JS.

  • Back-End Development: Develop and optimize server-side logic, databases, and RESTful APIs using .NET technologies.

  • Coordinate with outsourced development teams, providing technical guidance, code reviews, and ensuring that the projects align with the company’s standards and best practices.

  • Perform unit testing, integration testing, and debugging to ensure code quality and stability.

  • Create and maintain comprehensive documentation for technical specifications, development processes, and deployment strategies.

Your profile

  • You have a bachelor’s degree in computer science or the equivalent experience.

  • You have at least 3 years’ experience in a similar function

  • You have excellent knowledge of French or Dutch and a command of the other national language and are comfortable working in English.

  • You are proficient in Angular/AngularJS. You have strong understanding of .NET frameworks, C#, RESTful API development and SOAP webservices

  • You have a strong expertise in relational databases like SQL Server.

  • You are proficient in Git for version control, including experience with branching, merging, and pull requests.

  • You have basis knowledge of IA to accelerate your analysis and development

  • You have very good analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • You can communicate with all kinds of interlocutor as business analyst, tester and outsourced developer.

  • You are autonomous and quick to take the initiative.

  • You are passionate in IT and always curious to discover new things (technologies, business,… ). You are driven by the objectives rather than the means to reach them.

Good reasons to join us.

  • A permanent employment contract.

  • A company on a human scale within a dynamic group where you can rapidly have an impact.

  • Accessible management close to staff and a pleasant working environment.

  • Many opportunities for development, thanks in particular to our Athora Academy.

  • Balance between professional life and private life with generous holidays (at least 39 days a year), flexible working hours and up to 3 days’ teleworking a week.

  • An attractive salary package plus various fringe benefits.

  • Modern, bright offices conducive to collaboration.

  • A central location in the Porte de Namur district, accessible by train and public transport and with parking facilities available if needed.

  • Last but not least… a sunny terrace, afterworks between colleagues, teambuildings, an annual staff day and many other events to discover… 😉

If you are looking for a friendly organisation with a human face and attach value to cooperation and helping one another, you have come to the right address.

Boys & Girls Clubs of Northeast Ohio (BGCNEO) has an immediate opening for a Food Program Manager to be a key member of our Food Service Operations Team.

The Food Program Manager is responsible for the Club’s day-to-day food service program. The position directs food service personnel at our Cleveland area Broadway Club Kitchen (or as needed). This location serves multiple sites, to ensure functions are performed in a safe efficient manner meeting all food service regulations, provides written support to convey information, ensure proper transportation and availability of food service items to all sites. The Program Manager oversees preparation of Club meals, maintains adequate supplies and other kitchen materials, menu preparation, record keeping, maintaining a clean and sanitary workspace, and general overall supervision of food preparation services for BCGNEO.

This position reports to and receives work direction from the Food Service Compliance Manager to support Boys & Girls Clubs of Northeast Ohio.

This position is based out of our Broadway Club in Cleveland, Ohio.

Schedule is Full-Time, Monday through Friday, approximate 30 hours/ week. Schedule is generally 9:00 am to 3:00 pm but may occasionally vary.

Starting Pay Rate range is $ 21/ hour (commensurate with experience) and includes generous PTO. Benefits are also available.

KEY DUTIES and RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Responsible for preparation and implementation of the menu cycle at minimal cost and maximum efficiency.
  • Responsible for preparation of food by following proper sanitation, safety guidelines, regulations, and standards.
  • Coordinate and facilitate daily meal deliveries in a safe and timely manner.
  • Assist with procurement, prep, delivery, and storage of all food/food related items.
  • Responsible for insuring and maintaining freshness and safety of all food.
  • Always maintain a sanitary and safe kitchen as outlined by ODJFS and Board of Health.
  • Responsible for daily temperature recordings of food for meal service and cold storage
  • Track daily number of meals served, menu preparation and postings
  • Report program information as needed and required to the Food Program Compliance Manager to maintain program standards.
  • Maintain upkeep and service of all kitchen equipment and report any incidents or malfunction of kitchen equipment to Director.
  • Attend and assist with nutrition education programming/training as needed for compliance.
  • Participate in meetings regarding the Food Program as needed.
  • Supervise and provide instruction to food program/kitchen staff as needed
  • Responsible for ordering milk and assisting with ordering food and supplies for meal preparation when needed.
  • Reconcile vendor invoices with receivables weekly.
  • Assist with maintaining internal compliance policies, procedures and guidelines that align with regulatory requirements and industry best practices,

SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE and REQUIREMENTS:

  • Minimum of (3) years of experience working in an environment with high volume cooking
  • Experience with supervision of kitchen staff
  • Knowledge of kitchen operations and food preparation required.
  • Work independently and as part of a team
  • Organized and dependable.
  • High School diploma /GED required
  • (4) year education in Nutrition/Dietary or related field (preferred)
  • SERV Safe certified required.
